title: Calling overridable methods from constructors
answer: Yes, a constructor can call an overridable instance method, and normal dynamic dispatch can invoke the subclass override even while the superclass constructor is still running. The subclass's fields may not yet have completed their own initialization, so the override can observe default or inconsistent state. This is why constructors should generally avoid calling methods designed for overriding; use private, final, or static initialization helpers when appropriate.
